breakdown (min/day)","hideWhenNoData":true},"glossary_md":{"type":"splunk.markdown","options":{"backgroundColor":"rgba(15,17,23,0.50)","markdown":"### About these metrics
- **Body Battery** — Garmin's 0–100 estimate of your energy reserve, charging with rest and draining with stress/activity. **↑ higher is better**; the daily high/low band shows how much you recharged vs spent.
- **Stress** — all-day stress score (0–100) from heart-rate variability. **↓ lower is better**; brief spikes are normal, sustained highs aren't.
- **Respiration** — breaths per minute, split into **Sleep** and **Waking**. **Context** — a lower, stable sleeping rate is generally a good sign.
- **HRV** — overnight heart-rate variability (ms). **↑ higher is generally better** — a sign of recovery and autonomic balance (compare to your own baseline).
- **Resting HR** — your lowest steady heart rate (bpm). **↓ lower is generally better** as an aerobic-fitness proxy.
- **Fitness age** — Garmin's estimate of your aerobic fitness expressed as an age (VO2max-driven). **↓ lower is better** — reads younger than your real age is the goal (compare on the Heart page).
- **Intensity minutes** — minutes of Moderate + Vigorous activity; Garmin/WHO target is ~150/week. **↑ higher is better** (vigorous counts double toward the goal).
- **Daily heart-rate range** — your lowest and highest heart rate each day (min ≈ resting, max = peak effort). **Context** — a lower resting floor is a fitness sign; the max reflects your hardest effort that day.
- **Floors climbed** — flights of stairs / elevation gained per day. **↑ more is generally better** — incidental activity that adds up.
- **Time breakdown** — how your day splits across Highly active / Active / Sedentary / Sleeping minutes. **Less sedentary + more active is the goal** (the current day fills in as it's recorded).

_Garmin-specific signals. VO2max shows only if your device reports it._

**Some Garmin metrics are off by default on the watch.** If a Garmin signal is missing here or on Wellness → Vitals, check the device before suspecting ingest — **Pulse Ox (SpO₂)** ships **off** on many models, **Body Battery/stress** needs all-day heart-rate tracking, and **HRV status** needs ~3 weeks of consistent overnight wear on a supported sensor. [How to enable each one](https://github.com/narwhaldc/TA-garmin/blob/main/INSTALL.md#a-metric-is-missing-check-the-watch-first-not-the-pipeline) — none of it is retroactive, so data starts when you turn it on.

**Learn more:** [Garmin — Body Battery](https://www.garmin.com/en-US/garmin-technology/health-science/body-battery/)"}},"bb_sv_x":{"type":"splunk.singlevalue","title":"Body Battery
